newsitem.title: USA: PHLX plans to list options on Euro currency.
newsitem.headline: PHLX plans to list options on Euro currency.

text.p: The Philadelphia Stock Exchange plans to list customized and standardized options on the Euro, pending approval by the Securities Exchange Commission.
In a White Paper released on Thursday, the exchange said it would also continue to trade options on currencies that did not participate in the single European currency.
Under the terms of the Maastricht treaty, a single currency, the Euro, is scheduled to be introduced on January 1, 1999 for member countries of the European Community.

"While the move towards a single European currency is not proposed to begin until January 1999, the impact EMU may have on select PHLX long-term expiration currency options is rapidly approaching," Joseph Rizzello, PHLX executive vice president, said in a statement.
"We believe it is important for us to bring this critical issue to the forefront to help our customers and market users prepare for the pending EMU."
The exchange plans to file for Securities and Exchange Commission approval of the contract within the next few weeks, a spokeswoman said.

The exchange currently trades standardized options on 10 currency pairs and customized options on any combination of the Australian dollar, British pound, Canadian dollar, German mark, European Currency Unit, French franc, Japanese yen, Swiss franc, Italian lira, Spanish peseta and U.S. dollar.
